title: Getting dressed by myself
keyIdea: Getting dressed goes in an order: what goes next to your skin goes on first, so pants before trousers, socks before shoes, and the coat last. The label on a top goes at the back. Shoes go on the right feet. Have a go yourself, and ask a grown-up to help with just the tricky bit.
familyTip: Lay clothes out in the order they go on, like a train: pants, then trousers, then socks. Cut a sticker in half and put one half inside each shoe, so the halves make a whole picture when the shoes are on the right feet. Give time to try before you help.

visual.caption: On first or on later? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: dress a child inside layers first, spot tops on back to front, swap shoes to the right feet, button from the bottom, order the coat flip.

kid: Pants go on first. Then trousers go over them. Socks go on first. Then shoes go over them. The coat goes on last.
Find the label on your top. The label goes at the back. If you can see it at the front, turn the top round.
Shoes have a left and a right. Put half a sticker in each shoe. When the halves make a smiley, they are on the right feet.
Do buttons from the bottom, one hole at a time. If a bit is tricky, try first. Then ask a grown-up to help with that bit.
adult: Ages 3 to 4. In the EYFS, Development Matters (2021) asks children of this age to become more independent in meeting their own care needs, including dressing, and the Early Learning Goal for Managing Self expects them to manage their own basic needs, including dressing. Key words: first, next, last, front, back, left, right, inside out.

Make it easy to succeed. Choose elastic waists, big buttons and shoes with a strap. Lay clothes out in order, and start with undressing, which is easier. Do the coat flip: lay the coat on the floor inside up, stand by the hood, push both arms in and flip it over the head.

Common mistakes: putting outer clothes on before inner ones, like shoes before socks; wearing a top back to front with the label at the front; shoes on the wrong feet; buttons in the wrong holes, so the coat is wonky; and a grown-up doing it all. Be careful to help with only the tricky part, such as starting a zip, and let your child do the rest.

In the lab your child drags clothes onto a child in the right order, sorts tops into ready to go or turn it round, swaps a pair of shoes until the sticker halves make a smiley, does up a coat from the bottom button, and puts the four steps of the coat flip in order.

practice.prompt: Socks or shoes: which go on first?
practice.hint: Which one goes next to your feet?
practice.explain: Socks go next to your feet, so they go on first. Shoes go over the socks.

practice.prompt: A coat has {n} buttons. You have done the bottom one. How many buttons are left to do?
practice.hint: Count the buttons. Take away the one you have done.
practice.explain: {n} buttons take away the 1 you have done leaves {=n-1} to do, going up one at a time.

practice.prompt: You have {n} socks on the floor. Socks come in pairs, one for each foot. How many feet can you dress with them?
practice.hint: One sock goes on one foot. How many socks are there?
practice.explain: Each sock goes on one foot, so {n} socks dress {n} feet. Then the shoes go on over them.

practice.prompt: You can see the label at the front of your top. What do you do?
practice.explain: The label goes at the back. If it is at the front, the top is back to front, so turn it round.

practice.prompt: The sticker halves in your shoes do not make a smiley. What does that tell you?
choices: The shoes are on the wrong feet
practice.hint: When are the two halves next to each other?
practice.explain: The halves only make a smiley when the shoes are on the right feet. Swap them.

pool.prompt: Pants or trousers: which go on first?
pool.hint: Which one goes next to your skin?
pool.explain: Pants go next to your skin, so they go on first. Trousers go over them.

pool.prompt: What goes on last when you go out in the cold?
pool.hint: Which one goes over everything else?
pool.explain: The coat goes over everything, so it goes on last.

pool.prompt: Which button do you do first on a coat?
choices: The top one, then skip some
pool.hint: Start where the two sides of the coat line up best.
pool.explain: Start at the bottom and go up one hole at a time, so each button goes in the hole next to it.

pool.prompt: You put on pants, trousers and socks. Then you put on {n} more things. How many things are you wearing?
pool.hint: Count the 3 things, then count on {n} more.
pool.explain: 3 things and {n} more makes {=3+n} things on.

pool.prompt: Your zip will not start. What can you do?
choices: Try, then ask for help with that bit
Wait for a grown-up to do it all
pool.hint: Have a go first. Who can help with the tricky part?
pool.explain: Try first, then ask a grown-up to help start the zip. You can pull it up yourself.

pool.prompt: For the coat flip, where do you stand?
choices: By the bottom of the coat
pool.hint: The hood ends up at the back of your neck.
pool.explain: Stand by the hood, push your arms in and flip the coat over your head.

pool.prompt: Leo put his shoes on, then tried to put his socks on. What went wrong?
pool.hint: Which goes next to your feet?
pool.explain: Socks go next to your feet, so they go on before shoes. Leo has to take his shoes off and start again.

pool.prompt: A coat has {n} buttons. How many holes does it need?
pool.hint: Each button goes in its own hole.
pool.explain: Each button needs one hole, so {n} buttons need {n} holes.

pool.prompt: Where does the label on a top go?
pool.hint: You should not see it when you look down.
pool.explain: The label goes at the back, at the neck.
